job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: In our science club today, we analyzed the history of India's lunar exploration. We learned that Chandrayaan-1 was a major milestone, but it did not carry a rover; instead, it used the M3 instrument, provided by NASA, to detect water molecules trapped in lunar soil. This is very different from liquid water; it exists only as trace amounts of ice or hydrated minerals in shadowed regions. Moving to Chandrayaan-2, we discussed the landing sequence. Unlike on Earth, where thick atmospheres allow the use of parachutes to create drag, the Moon has no atmosphere. Therefore, the Vikram lander had to use retro-rockets to reduce its speed for a soft landing. We also clarified that while the Vikram lander faced challenges, the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter remained operational in its orbit, continuing to send valuable data back to Earth. Finally, we looked at Chandrayaan-3, which successfully touched down near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023. This mission proved that India could achieve a controlled landing, with the Pragyan rover performing experiments for one lunar day before its mission concluded. These missions show that lunar exploration requires precise engineering to overcome the lack of atmosphere and the harsh conditions of the lunar surface.

items.evidence: We learned that Chandrayaan-1 was a major milestone, but it did not carry a rover; instead, it used the M3 instrument, provided by NASA, to detect water molecules trapped in lunar soil.
items.q: Chandrayaan-1 detected water molecules in lunar soil. How did it do this?
options: Using the M3 instrument that NASA provided
Using a rover that drove across the soil
Using the M3 instrument that ISRO built itself
Using a probe that tested soil for months
items.explain: Chandrayaan-1 carried no rover. It used the M3 instrument, which NASA provided, to detect water molecules in lunar soil.

wrong.why: thinks ISRO built the M3 instrument
thinks the impact probe kept working on the Moon for months

items.evidence: This is very different from liquid water; it exists only as trace amounts of ice or hydrated minerals in shadowed regions.
items.q: Asha thinks astronauts could drink from lakes on the Moon. What does the lesson say about Moon water?
options: It exists only as tiny traces of ice or minerals
It forms big lakes inside deep craters
It stays as liquid pools in shadowed regions
It is clean enough to drink straight away
items.explain: Moon water is not liquid. It exists only as trace amounts of ice or hydrated minerals in shadowed regions.

wrong.why: thinks Chandrayaan-1 found lakes of water
thinks liquid water can stay on the Moon's surface
thinks Moon water is ready-to-drink water

items.evidence: Unlike on Earth, where thick atmospheres allow the use of parachutes to create drag, the Moon has no atmosphere.
items.q: Why did the Vikram lander use retro-rockets and not parachutes to slow down?
options: The Moon has no air for parachutes to push
Parachutes would tear in the Moon's thick air
Parachutes work there but rockets land faster
The Moon's gravity is too strong for parachutes
items.explain: Parachutes need a thick atmosphere to create drag. The Moon has no atmosphere, so Vikram used retro-rockets instead.

wrong.why: reverses the fact and thinks the Moon has thick air
thinks parachutes can slow a lander on the Moon
makes up a gravity reason that the passage never gives

items.evidence: We also clarified that while the Vikram lander faced challenges, the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter remained operational in its orbit, continuing to send valuable data back to Earth.
items.q: Raj says Chandrayaan-2 was a total failure. Which fact shows he is wrong?
options: Its orbiter kept sending useful data to Earth
Its orbiter crashed but sent one last photo
Its Vikram lander used parachutes to land safely
Its rover drove on the Moon for many years
items.explain: Vikram faced problems, but the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter stayed working in orbit and kept sending valuable data to Earth.

wrong.why: thinks the orbiter crashed along with Vikram
thinks parachutes work on the Moon
thinks a rover worked for years and mixes up the missions

items.evidence: This mission proved that India could achieve a controlled landing, with the Pragyan rover performing experiments for one lunar day before its mission concluded.
items.q: Meena wants to see Pragyan's new Moon experiments next year. Why is that not possible?
options: Its mission ended after one lunar day
Its signals are blocked on the far side
It crashed while landing near the south pole
It was carried by Chandrayaan-1, now retired
items.explain: Pragyan did experiments for only one lunar day before its mission ended, so it is not doing new experiments.

wrong.why: thinks Chandrayaan-3 landed on the far side
ignores that the passage calls the landing controlled and successful
